title: Keep one, fairly, without looking ahead
hook: Pick a fair item from a stream when you don't know how long it is.

doesNotKnow: that you can pick a uniform random item from a stream of unknown length in one pass

misconception: To choose a fair item from a stream you must store the whole stream first, or favour early items.
objective: The learner can explain that replacing the kept item with item i at chance 1/i leaves every item with the same final chance, because item 1 survives 1/2 x 2/3 x 3/4 = 1/4 and each later item has a smaller chance to get in but fewer draws to survive.

claims.text: With the rule 'item i replaces the kept one with chance 1/i', item 1 survives a 4-item stream with chance 1/2 x 2/3 x 3/4 = 1/4.
claims.source: Item 1 is still kept after arrival i exactly when draw i fails, chance 1 - 1/i = (i - 1)/i; the draws are independent, so the product for i = 2, 3, 4 is 1/2 x 2/3 x 3/4 = 1/4. Builder's node script (2026-10-14, algo2-sc) reproduces the exact distribution. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node exact distribution: item 1 survives 1/2 x 2/3 x 3/4 = 1/4; stage CHAIN builds '1 x 1/2 x 2/3 x 3/4'; reveal matches.

claims.text: After i items have arrived, every one of them is the kept item with chance exactly 1/i, so after 4 every bar is at 1/4.
claims.source: Induction: if each of items 1..i-1 is kept with chance 1/(i-1), then after arrival i item i is kept with chance 1/i and each older item with 1/(i-1) x (i-1)/i = 1/i. Builder's exact enumeration: after 2 [1/2, 1/2], after 3 [1/3 x3], after 4 [1/4 x4]. The stage bars are computed from this, not simulated. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node exact enumeration: after 2 [1/2,1/2], after 3 [1/3 x3], after 4 [1/4 x4]; stage bars are 1/k for arrived items (computed, not simulated).

claims.text: Each later item had a smaller chance to get in, but fewer draws left to survive.
claims.source: Item i enters with chance 1/i (smaller for larger i) and must then survive draws i+1..n, with chance i/n; the product is 1/n for every i. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Derivation holds: entry 1/i times survival i/n = 1/n; reveal sentence matches.

claims.text: 1,000 seeded streams of 4 kept items 1, 2, 3 and 4 236, 250, 257 and 257 times.
claims.source: Builder's node script and TALLY in Demo.tsx: mulberry32(1), 1,000 streams, draw rng() < 1/i for i = 2, 3, 4. The reveal and stage quote the TALLY constant, not hard-coded numbers. Expected about 250 each, standard deviation about 13.7. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own re-implementation of mulberry32(1) with Demo.tsx loop: TALLY 236, 250, 257, 257; chi-square 1.18; SD sqrt(1000 x 1/4 x 3/4) = 13.7. Reveal and stage quote TALLY.

claims.text: The shown stream uses seed 1: item 2 draws 0.627 (kept item stays 1), item 3 draws 0.003 (replaces it), item 4 draws 0.527 (item 3 stays).
claims.source: Disclosed seed (pattern disclose-chosen-seeds): seed 1 was the first seed tried and was not selected for its result. The spec's placeholder seed 7 was rejected because its tallies (257, 247, 249, 247; chi-square 0.27) look flatter than a typical run. Seed 1's chi-square is 1.18; across seeds 1-200 the median is 2.41 (builder's node script). The 1,000 streams start from the same seed, so the shown stream is the first of them. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node: seed 1 draws 0.627 (keep 1), 0.003 (keep 3), 0.527 (keep 3); stage shows 'seed 1'. Seed 7 tallies 257, 247, 249, 247 (chi-square 0.27) reproduce. Minor: my median chi-square over seeds 1-200 is 2.39, not 2.41 (source text only; not learner-facing).

claims.text: The rule holds one item in memory and never needs to know the stream's length.
claims.source: The state is the kept item and the count i of items seen; each step uses only i and the new item. Algorithm R with a reservoir of size 1: Vitter 1985, 'Random sampling with a reservoir', ACM TOMS 11(1); Knuth, TAOCP vol. 2, section 3.4.2 (citations from memory, not opened; check before publishing). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Holds from the code (state = kept item + count). Vitter, 'Random sampling with a reservoir', ACM TOMS 11(1):37-57, March 1985 confirmed by search-result text only (dl.acm.org blocked); Knuth TAOCP vol. 2 sec. 3.4.2 (Algorithm R) not opened, from my own knowledge. Learner sentence does not depend on either.

recall.question: Keeping one item from a stream, you replace it with item i at chance 1/i. With 10 items, what is item 1's final chance?
recall.why: Item 1 survives 1/2 x 2/3 x ... x 9/10 = 1/10; the product telescopes, so every item ends with 1/n.
